findings.title: Multi-step booking wizard has no browser-back / gesture-back contract
findings.principle: Any multi-step flow that is implemented as in-memory state rather than separate routes (the booking wizard) must intercept the browser/gesture back navigation the same way it intercepts the in-app exit control: either push one history entry per step so physical back steps the wizard back logically, or attach a popstate/beforeunload guard that shows the same 'leave this booking?' confirmation the X button already shows. A step transition that is invisible to the browser's own history stack is not a complete step.
findings.why: The wizard already treats losing progress as serious enough to earn a dedicated confirm-guard component for one exit path (the X button). If the physical back button or an edge-swipe (both standard mobile gestures) silently discard the same in-progress selections with zero warning, the product is inconsistent about how much it protects the same user state, and the inconsistency is invisible until a real user swipes back mid-flow and loses everything with no way to know it happened.
findings.local_evidence: components-legacy/booking/BookingWizard.tsx:115 reads currentStep/goToStep from useBooking() (React context state only); lib/booking-context.tsx has zero occurrences of popstate, sessionStorage, or localStorage (grepped, no hits); components-legacy/booking/BookingExitButton.tsx implements a 'leave this booking?' confirm guard (its own doc-comment cites Fresha IMG_4831) but that guard fires only on the explicit X click, never on router-level navigation; _docs/FRONTEND.md:293 documents that ONLY step-1's in-app back arrow does router.back(), steps 2+ use an in-app goToStep() with no browser-history entry at all.
findings.absence_proof: grep -rli 'beforeunload\|browser back\|physical back\|popstate' _design-system _rules _docs CLAUDE.md -> zero hits anywhere in the law estate. grep -n 'popstate\|router.push\|router.replace\|history.push\|beforeunload' lib/booking-context.tsx -> zero hits.
findings.existing_coverage: partial: LOCKFILE.md locks 'One progress indicator per screen... back arrow is the navigation' (booking stepper explicitly has no separate progress bar) and BookingExitButton covers the explicit-exit case, but neither text nor code addresses the browser/OS-level back gesture as a distinct interruption path.
findings.where_it_should_live: _design-system/LOCKFILE.md (booking flow row) + a new short section in _docs/FRONTEND.md's Wizard controller subsection (currently _docs/FRONTEND.md:282-301)
findings.enforcement: gate: a Playwright check in the booking flow test that does browser.goBack() at step 2/3 and asserts either the same 'leave this booking?' guard fires or the step correctly reverts; checklist item otherwise

findings.title: Two contradictory not-found.tsx files ship in the same app tree
findings.principle: There is exactly ONE 404 experience for the whole app, defined once, and every not-found.tsx file in the route tree (root and every nested segment) must render it, not a hand-rolled variant. A repo may never contain two not-found.tsx files with different copy, different layout, or different i18n treatment; a duplicate is drift the moment it is written, not just the moment it is seen.
findings.why: app/[locale]/not-found.tsx is the LOCKFILE-approved, i18n'd, gradient-404 design that explicitly documents itself as superseding an older icon-disc layout (comment: 'Supersedes the V3-D311 icon-disc layout'). app/not-found.tsx (the root, non-localized file) still IS that superseded icon-disc layout, verbatim: hardcoded German copy with no useTranslations(), and an em dash in the body text. Both rules it breaks (rule 33b 'NEVER hardcode user-facing text', taste rule 10 'no em-dashes anywhere in UI copy') are pinned, high-visibility rules in CLAUDE.md, yet this file sits unexamined because nobody's drift check looks at the app root, only app/[locale]/**.
findings.local_evidence: app/not-found.tsx (10 lines) hardcodes 'Diese Seite wurde leider nicht gefunden , vielleicht wurde sie umgestylt?' with a literal em dash and no locale awareness or Link-locale-prefix, next to app/[locale]/not-found.tsx which is i18n'd via useTranslations('errors') and carries an explicit doc-comment naming the LOCKFILE section it implements (LOCKFILE §15.3) and the exact pattern it supersedes.
findings.absence_proof: grep -rli 'canonical.*404\|single.*not-found\|not-found.*canonical' _design-system _rules -> zero hits (only unrelated hits in SUGGESTIONS.md/_pending-migration.md on other topics). grep -n '404\|not-found' _design-system/REMOVED.md _design-system/TASTE_LOG.md -> zero hits, so this duplicate was never logged as a decision either way. grep -n 'app/not-found' _design-system/_drift-report.md _design-system/_rebuilt_routes.json -> zero hits, confirming the drift-checker's route inventory never touched the root file.
findings.existing_coverage: partial: the intended 404 design IS locked (LOCKFILE §15.3, referenced from app/[locale]/not-found.tsx's own comment) but nothing states that ALL not-found.tsx files in the tree must implement it, and the drift/rebuilt-routes tooling that would have caught the stale duplicate never scans the app root.
findings.where_it_should_live: _rules/I18N_ROUTING.md Rule 36 (currently says only 'the not-found.tsx component MUST follow the current design system', singular, doesn't name the root file) + _design-system/_rebuilt_routes.json should include app/not-found.tsx
findings.enforcement: gate: extend the drift-checker's route inventory to include app/not-found.tsx and app/**/not-found.tsx, not just app/[locale]/**; a one-line diff check between the two files would have caught this immediately

findings.title: Auth-interrupt login redirect does not universally preserve the user's destination
findings.principle: Every place that redirects an unauthenticated user to /auth/login because they attempted a gated action (not a generic 'login' nav click) MUST append `?redirect=<the page or the specific action's return path>`, using the encodeURIComponent'd current pathname, exactly as the majority of /profile/* server pages already do. A login redirect with no `redirect=` param is only acceptable when the user explicitly navigated to a generic auth entry point (a 'Log in' menu link), never when their own in-context action (save, book, look up) is what triggered the redirect.
findings.why: This project already got most of this right: 18 of 19 /profile/* pages use a server-side redirect() with an encoded `redirect=` param, and the login page (components-legacy/auth/SignIn.tsx:30-49) correctly reads it back and validates it's an internal relative path before honoring it (open-redirect protection is already solved). The remaining three call sites are exactly the highest-friction ones: a user hearting a look, looking up a booking by code, or opening an intake form gets bounced to a blank login screen and, after authenticating, lands on the homepage instead of back where they were, forcing them to re-find and redo the action that prompted login in the first place.
findings.local_evidence: app/[locale]/inspo/page.tsx:362 `const handleAuthRequired = () => router.push(`/${locale}/auth/login`);` (no redirect param) , this exact gap was already flagged once in _design-system/research/PSYCH_AUDIT_2026-07-07.md:368 and is still unfixed 19 days later (today 2026-07-26). app/[locale]/booking/lookup/page.tsx:436 links to `/${locale}/auth/login` with no redirect param. app/[locale]/profile/intake-forms/page.tsx:48 `router.push(`/${locale}/auth/login`)` with no redirect param. Contrast: app/[locale]/profile/bookings/page.tsx:30, edit/page.tsx:31, favorites/page.tsx:27, haarprofil/page.tsx:28, settings/page.tsx:59, stamps/page.tsx:69, referral/page.tsx:72, and vouchers/page.tsx:71 all correctly build `redirect(...)` or `router.replace(...)` with an encoded redirect target.
findings.absence_proof: grep -rli 'preserve.*destination\|redirect param\|return.*url\|intended destination' _design-system _rules CLAUDE.md -> hits only in research/audit files (FRONTEND_AUDIT_2026-07-08.md, AUDIT_CHANGELIST_2026-07-07.md, PSYCH_AUDIT_2026-07-07.md, IG_PRINCIPLES_VERDICTS_2026-07-16.md) that flagged instances of this problem as findings, never a durable rule in _rules/ or LOCKFILE.md that would have caught the recurrence.
findings.existing_coverage: partial: the CORRECT pattern is already the majority convention (18/19 profile pages) and was independently flagged for the Inspo case by a July 7 audit, but the pattern was never promoted to a written rule, so the same defect exists in 3 places 3 weeks later and nothing stops a 4th.
findings.where_it_should_live: _rules/STRUCTURAL_RULES.md as a new numbered rule (adjacent to Pattern B, 'Auth Guard on Profile Fetches', STRUCTURAL_RULES.md:215-233), generalized beyond /api/profile fetches to every auth-required interrupt
findings.enforcement: checklist item in the same pre-commit checklist STRUCTURAL_RULES.md:173-193 already runs for new components; a grep-based lint rule flagging any `auth/login` push/redirect literal without an adjacent `redirect=` in the same statement would catch new instances mechanically

findings.title: Filter/facet state is URL-synced on /search but not on /inspo, so the same UI pattern is shareable on one surface and not the other
findings.principle: Any filter, facet, or drill-down selection that changes what a browse/discovery page shows MUST be reflected in the URL via router.replace (not push, to avoid polluting back-history per keystroke) the moment it is applied, on every browse surface in the app, not just /search. If a surface's filter state cannot be reconstructed from its URL alone, a refresh, a copy-pasted link, or the browser back button will silently show the user a different result set than the one they were looking at, and that is a correctness bug wearing a UX costume.
findings.why: Solen already solved this correctly once (SearchTemplate reads city/service/category/date/period/sort/open_now/instant_bookable/deals/walk_in/min_rating/min_price/max_price/gender/amenities/map/layout, all from searchParams) which proves the team knows the pattern and values it enough to wire a dozen params. Inspo's progressive drill-down filter is the newer, more actively-developed discovery surface (LOYALTY/DISCOVERY work is ongoing per project memory) and it silently regressed on exactly the property /search protects: sharing an Inspo link, refreshing mid-filter, or hitting back loses the gender/texture/style/cuts selections a user just made.
findings.local_evidence: app/[locale]/inspo/page.tsx:60-102 seeds ONLY `category` (line 60-62) and `search` (line 65) from searchParams; `activeFilters` (line 69, drives gender/texture/style), `cuts` (line 96), and the dnaGender/dnaTexture/dnaLength pre-seed state (lines 100-102) are plain useState with no URL sync. grep -n 'router.replace|router.push' on the same file (only 5 hits, all page-to-page navigation, e.g. line 319/322/458/474) confirms no call ever writes filter state back into the URL. Contrast: app/[locale]/_components/search/SearchTemplate.tsx:437-521 reads 15+ distinct filter params from searchParams.get(...).
findings.absence_proof: grep -rli 'filter state.*url\|url.*shareab\|shareable.*filter\|filter.*shareable' _design-system _rules -> one hit (COMPONENT_REGISTRY.md), unrelated context (not a URL-state rule). grep -rn 'sessionStorage|scrollY' on inspo/page.tsx and search/page.tsx -> zero hits either way (state persistence generally is not addressed for either surface, see finding ia-navigation-05).
findings.existing_coverage: none as a stated rule; SearchTemplate's own code is the only 'coverage', and it is not written down anywhere as a cross-surface requirement, so a new browse surface (as Inspo's drill-down filter shows) has no reason to follow it.
findings.where_it_should_live: _design-system/LOCKFILE.md nav row (currently only covers DateTimePicker, breadcrumb, tabs) or a new row; alternately _rules/STRUCTURAL_RULES.md as a companion to Rule 32 (Inspo routing)
findings.enforcement: gate: a Playwright check per browse surface that applies a filter, reads window.location.search, reloads the page, and asserts the filter UI still shows the applied state

findings.title: No scroll-restoration law or implementation exists anywhere in the app
findings.principle: Any list/grid page a user can navigate away from and back to (search results, Inspo feed, saved items) must restore the user's exact scroll position on back-navigation, not reset to top. This is implemented via a scroll-position cache keyed by pathname+querystring (sessionStorage or Next's own scroll-restoration primitive), restored in a layout-level effect, not left to the browser's default (which App Router's client-side transitions do not reliably preserve).
findings.why: Losing scroll position on back-navigation from a detail page to a list is one of the most common, most-noticed navigation papercuts in any browse-then-inspect product (this is literally the 'return-to-spot' task class Nielsen Norman group names for infinite scroll specifically). Solen's own psychology research already identified this as a high-confidence, sourced fix ('infinite scroll... hurts... return-to-spot tasks... preserve scroll position on Search back-nav', NN/g cited) but the recommendation stayed inside a research document and was never implemented or promoted into an enforced rule.
findings.local_evidence: grep -n 'sessionStorage|scrollY|scrollTop|scroll position' on app/[locale]/search/page.tsx and app/[locale]/inspo/page.tsx -> zero hits on both. grep -n 'scrollRestoration' next.config.js/.ts -> zero hits (Next's experimental scroll-restoration flag is not enabled). components-legacy/layout/PageTransitionWrapper.tsx and PageTransition.tsx (the global route-transition wrapper used by every page, STRUCTURAL_RULES.md Pattern C) contain zero references to scroll at all, confirming no global mechanism exists to fall back on.
findings.absence_proof: grep -rli 'scroll restoration' _design-system _rules -> zero hits. The only place this concept appears in the whole estate is _design-system/research/PSYCH_CONVERSION.md:160 and PSYCH_PSYCHOLOGY.md:199, both research/recommendation documents, never promoted to LOCKFILE, SOURCE.md, or a _rules file.
findings.existing_coverage: partial: a specific, sourced recommendation exists in two research docs (high confidence rated) but was never implemented and never became an enforced or even checklist-level rule; the recommendation and the current code have simply never been reconciled.
findings.where_it_should_live: _design-system/LOCKFILE.md (new row) or _docs/FRONTEND.md as a cross-cutting navigation pattern, referencing PSYCH_CONVERSION.md:160 as the sourced rationale
findings.enforcement: checklist item first (cheap, no gate infra exists for scroll behavior yet); a manual verification step in the verifier-loop for any new list/detail pair

findings.title: No law governs what happens to a salon's URL when its slug would change
findings.principle: A salon's slug, once published, is either (a) permanently immutable, or (b) editable only through a flow that writes the OLD slug into a `salon_slug_redirects` table and serves a 301/permanentRedirect from every old slug to the current one, forever. Whichever is chosen must be written down before any UI ships that lets an owner rename their business, because renaming a business and changing its URL are two different actions that this system currently conflates by not addressing either.
findings.why: Salon slugs are the load-bearing identifier for every customer-facing surface named in this domain brief: bookmarked PDPs, shared booking links, walk-in queue QR codes, tip-sheet deep links, and every review/SEO backlink pointing at /salon/[slug]. If a future 'edit business name' feature (a completely reasonable, likely dashboard feature) silently regenerates the slug from the new name the way most slugify() helpers default to doing, every one of those external references 404s the instant it ships, with no redirect and no warning, and this would have zero test coverage because nothing currently exercises a slug change.
findings.local_evidence: app/api/salons/[slug]/route.ts:31-50 (the PATCH handler salon owners use to update their salon) resolves the row by UUID-or-slug but performs no slug regeneration itself today, so the immediate risk is latent, not live; however grep for a dedicated slug-editing route or a salon_slug_redirects-equivalent table found none: no `app/api/dashboard/salon/settings` route exists, and no slug-history/redirect table appears in _inventory/SURFACE.md's DB section.
findings.absence_proof: grep -rin 'slug' _design-system _rules _docs CLAUDE.md -> zero hits that discuss stability, renaming, or redirect behavior for slugs (all hits are either drift-report file paths or REMOVED.md entries about deleted duplicate ROUTES, not about slug mutability). grep -rli 'slug.*stab\|slug.*chang\|slug.*rename\|rename.*slug' _design-system _rules -> one hit, _design-system/research/FRONTEND_AUDIT_2026-07-08.md, which is a prior audit note, not a codified rule; confirmed the specific text there does not propose a redirect-table solution.
findings.existing_coverage: none: this is a genuine, unaddressed gap. The closest analog, Rule 32's permanentRedirect() requirement for deleted CATEGORY routes, establishes the project already believes in redirect-on-URL-change as a principle, it has just never been extended to entity slugs.
findings.where_it_should_live: _rules/STRUCTURAL_RULES.md as a new rule, or _docs/BACKEND.md next to the salons table documentation
findings.enforcement: doc-only law for now (no live editing surface to gate); becomes a hard PreToolUse-style review gate the moment any PR adds a salon-name-edit endpoint
findings.confidence: assume, since the live edit path does not exist yet so this cannot bite today; it is a landmine for the first name-edit feature, not a current production defect

findings.title: The dead-click/dead-link contract's static checker cannot see computed or templated hrefs, and this already produced a live dead link
findings.principle: The Clickable Surface Contract's route-existence check (SOURCE.md §11, pattern A: 'href routes to a real page') must extend beyond literal JSX `href="/x"` strings to any prop passed down that is later rendered as a Link/anchor href, by requiring the string template's static portion to be checked against the actual route manifest (every app/**/page.tsx path) at build or lint time, not only grepped as a literal.
findings.why: SOURCE.md already names its own blind spot in general terms ('a prop that's syntactically present but null at runtime... false negative') but does not name the specific, already-manifested failure mode: a computed href built from a template string (`` `/${locale}/bookings/${id}` ``) that points at a route which was never built. This is not hypothetical, it already happened and was caught by hand, not by tooling.
findings.local_evidence: _docs/FRONTEND.md:778 and :2051 both document, in identical language: 'DEAD LINK: RefundCaseView + UpchargeApproveView both receive receiptHref = /[locale]/bookings/[id]... but there is NO app/[locale]/bookings/[id]/page.tsx , that path falls through to the home shell.' This was found by a human audit, not by the drift-checker, and remains unfixed as of the current codebase state (the same two lines describe it as still-wired in the current file).
findings.absence_proof: grep -rli 'computed href\|template.*href\|dynamic href' _design-system _rules -> zero hits. SOURCE.md's own 'Limits of static checking' section (lines 779-784) names two other false-negative classes explicitly but never names this one, despite the concrete instance sitting 700+ lines earlier in the same document (FRONTEND.md:778, a sibling file in the same doc set).
findings.existing_coverage: partial: the general principle (a href must point to a real route) is locked and the document is honest that static checking has limits, but the specific computed-href failure mode is undocumented even though the project's own audit already found and recorded a live instance of exactly this failure.
findings.where_it_should_live: _design-system/SOURCE.md §11 'Limits of static checking' (SOURCE.md:779-784), adding this as a third named limit, plus a direct fix reference to _docs/FRONTEND.md:778
findings.enforcement: gate: extend solen-drift-check to build a route manifest from app/**/page.tsx and flag any string-template href/receiptHref/redirectTo prop whose static prefix does not match a manifest entry

findings.title: No single redirect policy for removed routes: three killed features got three different URL outcomes
findings.principle: When a route is killed, its outcome must be chosen from ONE named decision tree, not improvised per feature: (a) the concept moved and still exists under a new URL -> `permanentRedirect()` (308) to the new location; (b) the concept is gone but a nearby page is still the right landing spot -> a plain `redirect()` to that page; (c) the concept is entirely gone with no landing spot -> the route is deleted and MUST be added to `COMING_SOON_ROUTES`-style middleware list or otherwise produce the locked 404 page, never a bare unstyled Next.js default 404. Every REMOVED.md entry for a route deletion must state which of the three it chose and why.
findings.why: A user or bookmark hitting a killed route should get a predictable class of outcome (redirected forward, redirected to safety, or a designed 404), never a coin-flip depending on which engineer happened to delete that particular feature. Right now the SAME repo has all three outcomes live for three different killed features with no record of why each got a different treatment, which means the choice was never actually a choice, it was whatever felt convenient that day.
findings.local_evidence: app/[locale]/inspo/nails/page.tsx:9 `permanentRedirect(`/${locale}/inspo?category=nails`)` (outcome a, correctly matches Rule 32's own requirement). app/[locale]/profile/gift-cards/page.tsx:13 `redirect(`/${locale}/profile`)` (outcome b, a plain redirect to a parent page). The Pakete/packages feature (REMOVED.md:29, 'owner kill em all delete em 2026-06-13') has NO surviving page.tsx anywhere under app/[locale]/profile or app/[locale]/salon/[slug] (confirmed via find, zero results for *package* under either directory), meaning it falls through to the bare not-found chain (outcome c) with zero explicit routing decision ever made for it, just deletion.
findings.absence_proof: grep -rli 'redirect polic\|removed route\|route removal' _design-system _rules -> zero hits. Rule 32 (I18N_ROUTING.md:11-27) mandates permanentRedirect() but scopes itself explicitly to 'old category-specific discovery routes', not to route removal in general; nothing generalizes it.
findings.existing_coverage: partial: Rule 32 IS a redirect-policy rule, but only for one specific case (discovery category routes) and the graveyard protocol (REMOVED.md) requires logging WHAT was removed and WHY, but never requires logging WHICH of the three URL outcomes the removal chose, so REMOVED.md's own gift-cards and packages entries (lines cited above) don't record this dimension at all.
findings.where_it_should_live: _design-system/REMOVED.md's required entry format (extend the `npm run removed -- ...` template to require a redirect-outcome field) + _rules/STRUCTURAL_RULES.md as a generalized version of Rule 32
findings.enforcement: checklist item added to the graveyard-skip / pre-commit-graveyard.sh hook: a route deletion commit must state its redirect outcome in the REMOVED.md line it's already required to add

findings.title: No decision rule exists for when a piece of UI should be its own route versus a sheet/modal/component-state overlay
findings.principle: Before building any multi-step or substantial piece of interactive UI, name whether it is (a) a ROUTE (deep-linkable, back-button-navigable, indexable, survives refresh) because its content is shareable, bookmarkable, or worth returning to directly, or (b) a SHEET/MODAL (ephemeral, layered over a route, closes to the exact state the route was already in) because its content is transient and only makes sense in the context of the thing it was opened from. State the choice in the component's `_design-system/components/<Name>.md` Purpose section the same way Layer 1/2/3 is already required there.
findings.why: This project has already made this exact call correctly, more than once, but only ever as an implicit, undocumented precedent buried in individual decisions: reviews are '(modal over /[locale]/salon/[slug]/reviews)' (a real route, with a modal presentation layered on top so it's still deep-linkable), and the SalonServicesSheet was deliberately RETIRED in favor of deep-linking to /salon/[slug]/booking (REMOVED.md:86, 'now Alle ansehen deep-links to /salon/[slug]/booking'), showing the team's own bias is toward routes over sheets for substantial content. But the booking WIZARD itself (finding ia-navigation-01) makes the opposite choice, pure in-memory state with no route per step, for content that is arguably just as substantial and just as worth resuming. Nobody has ever written down the rule that would explain why these got different treatments, so the next engineer building the next multi-step flow has no way to make the same call the team already implicitly prefers.
findings.local_evidence: _docs/FRONTEND.md:1017 '(modal over /[locale]/salon/[slug]/reviews)' , the reviews modal sits over a real, addressable route. _design-system/REMOVED.md:86 documents the explicit 2026-07-19 owner decision to retire a full-screen sheet in favor of a route deep-link for the exact same content class (service selection) the booking wizard still keeps as pure state. components-legacy/booking/BookingWizard.tsx (per finding 01) keeps all 3-4 steps as one route with context state, the opposite choice.
findings.absence_proof: grep -rli 'modal vs route\|sheet vs route\|route vs modal\|route vs sheet' _design-system _rules -> zero hits. The only decision trees that exist in the whole estate are for VISUAL/color/elevation choices (SOURCE.md §14.0 color-layer decision tree, CONTROL_ELEVATION.md), never for the structural question of route-vs-overlay.
findings.existing_coverage: none as a written rule; the pattern exists only as scattered precedent (reviews modal, retired services sheet) that a new contributor has no way to discover or generalize from.
findings.where_it_should_live: _design-system/COMPONENT_REGISTRY.md, alongside the existing Layer 1/2/3 requirement (COMPONENT_REGISTRY.md:181), as a new mandatory 'Container: route | sheet | modal, because ___' declaration
findings.enforcement: checklist item in the same pre-commit checklist that already requires Layer 1/2/3 be named

findings.title: Query parameter names are reused with different meanings across features, risking silent collisions
findings.principle: A URL query parameter name carries exactly ONE meaning across the entire app. Once `category` means 'service taxonomy' on /search, no other route may use `category` to mean something else (a discovery vertical); if a second, genuinely distinct concept needs a similarly-named param, it gets a feature-scoped or explicitly disambiguated name (`discoveryCategory`, or a documented shared enum) instead of reusing the bare word.
findings.why: This project has already documented, as a named architectural fact, that discovery categories and salon/service categories are two different taxonomies that must never be joined directly ('discovery cats != salon cats; join direct = silent no-op; bridge hair->coiffeur, beard->barbershop', per project memory and the category taxonomy split). Having the URL layer use the same bare param name (`category`) for both taxonomies on two different routes is the exact kind of surface-level collision that makes the underlying, already-known semantic split easy to get wrong: copy a `category=nails` query string from an Inspo link into a /search-shaped context (or vice versa, e.g. a future shared search-and-discover surface) and it silently resolves against the wrong taxonomy instead of erroring.
findings.local_evidence: app/[locale]/_components/search/SearchTemplate.tsx:439 `const urlService = searchParams.get("service") ?? searchParams.get("category")` (category = a specific bookable service/taxonomy value here) and :471 `searchParams.get("gender")` (a service filter). app/[locale]/inspo/page.tsx:60-62 `searchParams?.get("category")` (category = one of the fixed DISCOVERY_CATEGORIES verticals, a different enum) and the same page's dnaGender concept (lines 100-102, component-state today per finding 04, but the same English word 'gender' names a different axis: hair-DNA demographic, not a service filter).
